real_conflicts: The proposal to move the 'Reserve Tickets' button to the top of the left column (clarity_hierarchy) would destroy the intentional narrative arc of the page. The current layout guides the eye from the atmospheric title down through the context to the action; placing a hard-edged UI element at the top would immediately break the immersive mood and make the page feel like a standard e-commerce landing page rather than an art exhibition.

The proposal to use a 'brighter, more saturated color' like warm gold for the button (brief_intent) would clash with the somber, monochromatic palette of 'absence' and 'memory.' A bright gold button would feel like a generic 'sale' alert, undermining the sophisticated, atmospheric identity of the piece.
accepted: The proposal to add a subtle 'glitch' or displacement effect to the exhibition title (my own previous revision) is accepted as a core requirement for the 'fragmented perception' theme.
The proposal to break the artwork's rectangular boundary (my own previous revision) is accepted to create the necessary spatial tension.
concession: I concede that the button needs to be more prominent than it currently is, but I reject the idea that this requires a bright, high-contrast color or a change in its vertical position that disrupts the reading flow.
compromise: Keep the button in its current position at the bottom of the text block to preserve the narrative flow, but apply the 'visual_system_craft' suggestion of a soft, pale outer glow (box-shadow) to make it feel like it is emitting light. This increases its prominence and ties it to the 'light' medium mentioned in the text without using a jarring, saturated color.
nonnegotiable: The artwork must break its hard rectangular frame (via clip-path or bleed) to visually represent the 'fragmented' nature of the exhibition; a static, contained image is a failure of the brief's artistic mandate.
